Your day at the park

Go slowly.
See more.

This is not a race through a checklist. Stay with the moment, watch the animals’ behavior, then make time for the hands-on stops after the drive.

01

Drive the safari route

Stay comfortable in your own vehicle as you move through natural viewing areas at your own pace.

02

Pause for the pack

Listen for the wolves, watch the foxes, and notice the social dynamics that are nearly impossible to catch in the wild.

03

Feed the trout

After the drive, step onto the fish-pond bridge and deck to feed golden, blue, and rainbow trout.

04

Meet the little ones

See seasonal wolf and fox pups, then visit the Animal Interaction Place for friendly farm animals.

Preservation in every detail 30+

Remarkable color variations within the red fox family—protected and cared for here.

Care & preservation

Wild lives deserve close care.

The park’s rare fox color lines and native wildlife are supported with attentive daily care, quality nutrition, fresh water, shelter, open space, and regular licensed veterinary checks.

Rare red-fox family colorsMore than the familiar rust coat—preserved for future generations.
Health-first husbandryConsistent observation and care centered on animal wellbeing.

Before you
head out.

Most visits take 1–2 hours, but the self-guided format lets you slow down and watch longer when the animals are active.

Yes during the safari drive. Afterward, you can step out for the fish-pond bridge, deck, and Animal Interaction Place.

The park is designed for reliable close viewing of animals that can be elusive in the wild. Like all animals, they still choose when to rest or move.

Yes. The 2026 season pass is $85 for ages 11+ and $55 for ages 3–10. Passes are non-transferable.

Yellowstone Safari Park is at 2246 W 4000 N in Rexburg, Idaho, a few minutes from Highway 20 and near the Teton River.
